speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when your gait imbalance and limb coordination issues first started, and have they been getting worse over time? Do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs as well?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of heavy alcohol use, or have you noticed any recent weight loss? Also, are you experiencing any headaches, vomiting, or changes in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your Crohn's disease and the use of natalizumab, have you recently experienced any fever, severe headaches, or a sudden worsening of your balance and coordination? I need to rule out an opportunistic infection like PML, so I will REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. Vital Signs: Temperature Normothermic, Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, and Respiratory Rate within normal range. Neurological Examination: Ataxic gait noted; Right Upper Limb Strength 4/5; Evidence of ataxia on coordination tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings confirming multifocal demyelinating lesions in a patient on natalizumab strongly indicate Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
